key_headlines.title: Real Estate War One Year Later: Luxury Housing Prices Fall While Mid-Range Properties Rise
key_headlines.summary: One year after the August 3 housing policy, only Gangnam's three districts saw price declines, while Seoul's outer regions experienced significant increases. Affordable housing prices climbed nearly 2 billion won, with districts like Seongbuk rising 16% and Dongdaemun up 12%.

key_headlines.title: Seoul's Top 10 Large Apartment Complexes Face Severe Jeonse Shortage
key_headlines.summary: Major complexes like Olleopa and Jamsil ELS show jeonse listings at only 3.6%, with Licents at just 0.9%, indicating near-complete disappearance of long-term rental supply due to real estate transaction regulations and supply shortages.

key_headlines.title: Government Plans 430,000 Electric Vehicles with 2 Trillion Won Subsidy Next Year
key_headlines.summary: To counter slowing EV demand and Chinese EV market entry, the government will expand electric vehicle purchase subsidies and launch an EV conversion campaign to lower purchase barriers and accelerate adoption rates.

key_headlines.title: Domestic Soybean Consumption Policy Retreats: Resumption of Additional Imports Planned
key_headlines.summary: The Ministry of Agriculture will resume additional soybean imports next year after halting them in February, responding to cost pressures from processing companies seeking conditional increases in import quantities.

key_headlines.title: Trump Administration to Revoke Tariff-Free Benefits for South Africa and Rwanda
key_headlines.summary: The Trump administration threatens to eliminate tariff-free trade benefits for South Africa and Rwanda, potentially eliminating up to 10,000 jobs in South Africa where unemployment exceeds 30%.

sections.Hot Economy News: South Korea's real estate market shows divergent trends one year after August 3 housing policies, with luxury properties in Gangnam declining while mid-range housing in outer Seoul districts surges significantly. The jeonse (long-term rental) market faces severe supply shortages, with major apartment complexes showing jeonse listings below 4%, threatening the foundation of housing affordability. Rental prices across Seoul have reached record highs, with outer districts now exceeding 1 million won monthly in some areas. These trends reflect rising household housing burden despite government efforts to stabilize prices. The disconnect between policy goals and market realities continues to challenge consumers seeking affordable housing options.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: South Korea's fiscal position is improving significantly, with next year's budget deficit ratio dropping to -0.1% of GDP and national debt declining from 51.6% to 48.3% of GDP. The government projects accomplishment of 1 trillion dollar exports and 40,000 dollar per capita income this year, supported by semiconductor sector recovery. Next year's corporate tax revenue is expected to increase by 113 trillion won, with 74% of the increase attributed to corporate taxes benefiting from semiconductor industry strength. However, the government must balance record investment levels with fiscal sustainability while addressing ongoing income polarization. Australia's central bank raised rates to 4.85% for the fifth time this year despite economic slowdown, prioritizing inflation control over growth concerns.
sections.Financial Markets: Foreign investors sold 22 trillion won in Korean stocks during October while retail investors increased US equity purchases, yet the Korean won strengthened due to robust export performance and foreign bond inflows. KOSPI and KOSDAQ opened higher but reversed into decline as foreign investors led massive selling, with KOSPI falling 2.43% and KOSDAQ dropping below 700. US 10-year Treasury yields remain elevated near 5% despite the Federal Reserve's rate hold, with 10-year yields at 4.96% and 30-year yields at 5.33%. Market volatility continues as investors position ahead of potential rate cuts while monitoring US midterm election results and geopolitical tensions. Capital flows remain sensitive to foreign investor sentiment and US economic data releases.
sections.Industry & Technology: South Korea has become globally competitive in semiconductors, nuclear power, automobiles, batteries, and shipbuilding—technologies now sought by global leaders including the US administration. The 12th Basic Power Supply Plan faces industry concerns about lower electricity demand projections, potentially threatening AI data center and semiconductor investments requiring stable power supply. Mercedes-Benz Korea must pay 4 million won per vehicle owner for failing to disclose battery manufacturer information to EV consumers. Government officials are actively promoting South Korea's semiconductor ecosystem to international partners, highlighting expansion plans for tech hubs like Yongin. Power infrastructure becomes critical as AI and advanced industries accelerate electricity demand.
sections.Real Estate: Yongin's semiconductor cluster expansion drives increased apartment supply, with 1,777 units from six complexes launched January-October 2026, supporting housing demand from industry growth. Gangnam reconstruction projects show "downsizing" trends as residents reduce floor area to decrease tax burdens while increasing refunds, with some 59 square meter units offering up to 1.5 billion won returns. GH launched Korea's first "equity accumulation division housing" with 240 units at Suwon Gwanggyo, requiring only partial payment at move-in with 5-year residency obligations. Seoul's rental market reached record highs with average apartment monthly rent at 166 million won, while outer districts like Nowon, Dobong, and Gangbuk exceeded 1 million won monthly. Sejong City leads provincial competition rates at 14.21 to 1, with 2,316 units in major complexes scheduled this month.
sections.International Economy: Trump administration policies on tariffs and trade threaten South Africa's export-dependent economy, with potential elimination of 10,000 jobs and loss of preferential tariff benefits affecting 30% unemployment rates. US midterm elections show economic discontent despite low unemployment and GDP growth, with voters expressing anger over tariffs, war costs, and inflation pressures in rural and small-town communities. Potential tariff increases and trade war escalation pose risks to global commerce, with fiscal deficit currently at 6% of GDP and pressure to reduce it to 3% creating policy tensions. Middle East tensions from Iran airstrikes initially spurred commodity price increases, though diplomatic resolution prospects tempered energy price volatility. International commodity markets remain sensitive to geopolitical developments and US policy uncertainty.
sections.AI & Economy: Industrial metals like copper and tin surge as AI infrastructure expansion drives semiconductor and electronics production, with tin prices rising 23% this year as Myanmar and Indonesia reduce mining output. AI investment concentration concerns emerge from both US and Chinese financial authorities, warning that excessive capital flows to data centers and AI equipment threaten traditional industries and increase financial risk. Tech giants including SpaceX, Microsoft, Alphabet, and Meta report strong Q3 results driven by AI infrastructure demand, with SpaceX's AI compute revenue exceeding 50% of divisional sales. Democrats potentially gaining midterm control could trigger comprehensive AI regulation legislation, potentially constraining Trump administration's data center deregulation and industry growth policies. South Korea Electric Power Society emphasizes electricity as core national competitiveness under AI and advanced industry expansion.
sections.Others: Law schools face criticism for continuing to fill openings with extra-quota students, effectively obsoleting transfer admission systems while increasing financial burden on students as universities seek revenue preservation. Industrial ministry launches AI factory expansion strategy with 650 billion won investment to spread successful AI models across manufacturing facilities, cooperation partners, and industrial complexes. Alteogen achieved record quarterly revenue and operating profit driven by expanded Keytruda subcutaneous injection sales and new technology licensing deals. US midterm election outcomes will significantly impact Korea-US relations, with particular attention to defense transfer of command and potential Coupang and nuclear submarine policy implications. Market research reveals hidden voter dissatisfaction uncaptured by standard polls, with economic grievances over prices and employment driving unexpected midterm results despite strong macroeconomic indicators.
